title: Observation-only round 3: dominant GetUserTweets probe is a fully-cached fixed-shape index access with no query_execution lever

anomaly.unit: fraction of the 960s terminal budget (8 terminals x 120s)

configuration_cause: The dominant transaction GetUserTweets is a read-only shared-buffer index access: buffer_hit_ratio 0.99992, seq_scan 0/s, idx_scan ~22.9k/s, blks_read 0.000743/txn, temp_bytes 0, and the observed plan is a single Index Scan (est_rows 1.0, est_cost 8.45). None of the allowed planner/statistics/executor knobs (default_statistics_target, from_collapse_limit, join_collapse_limit, random_page_cost, seq_page_cost, effective_cache_size, jit, work_mem, temp_buffers) can change the executor path or per-row cost of a fully-cached fixed-shape index probe, so the incumbent already sits at the query_execution optimum for this transaction class.
mechanism: Closed-loop identity TPS = terminals / weighted-mean client latency. GetUserTweets issues 3,186,707 of ~3,630,272 transactions (88%) and owns 0.8813 of the 960s terminal budget (846.1s). It is read-only and never enqueues on the WAL/commit path, so the flagged wal_wait cannot explain the read tail: write_average_ms is 0.138, wal_write_time is 30.45ms/s (~1.0us per client transaction), wal_sync is 0/s, host_io some/full stall fractions are 0.0, and wal_waiting_backends is median 0 / p95 0 / max 1 of ~9 backends. The dominant term is therefore governed by count and cached-probe latency, neither of which any allowed query_execution knob moves.
query_effect: GetUserTweets read path: ~7.23 rows fetched per transaction from shared buffers (9.62 blks_hit/txn, 7.43e-4 blks_read/txn, 7.18e-6 ms blk_read_time/txn, 0 temp bytes); p50 166us, mean 265.5us, p99 2626us, max 31294us. The tail is the executor/OS micro-stall on a hot cached page, not a data-access cost any planner knob can lower.
expected_tps_effect: unchanged: with knob_changes=[] the configuration is bit-identical to the incumbent, so goodput_rps stays inside the observed 28,257.5-31,906.7 rps band (verified median 30,213.6).
expected_latency_effect: unchanged: GetUserTweets p50 ~166us and p99 ~2626us are within the incumbent replicate spread (p50 165/169/157us; p99 2451/2486/2280/2626us).

predictions.rationale: Closed-loop identity 8 terminals / 270us weighted mean = 29.6k rps reproduces the measured 29,589 rps. With knob_changes=[] no query_execution lever is applied, so throughput must remain within +/-5% of the 29,762.6-31,906.7 verified replicate band.

0.8813 = 846.1s of 960s at 3,186,707 transactions; incumbent replicates were 0.8798/0.8817/0.8787 (span 0.30pp). With identical config neither the call count nor the cached-probe mean (265.5us) can move, so the fraction stays within 3pp of 0.881.

p50 166us is a shared-memory index access (buffer_hit_ratio 0.99992, 9.62 blks_hit/txn, 7.43e-4 blks_read/txn, 0 temp bytes) at plan cost 8.45; no allowed statistics/planner/executor knob alters this executor path, so p50 stays within the +/-10% replicate tolerance (165/169/157us).

p99 2626us is executor/OS micro-stall on hot cached pages with zero lock waits (locks_waiting 0/0/0), zero conflicts and zero JIT activity (plan cost 8.45 << default jit_above_cost); no query_execution knob governs this path, so p99 stays within +/-10% of the 2280-2626us replicate span.

Mean WAL write is 0.138ms at 220 writes/s with host_io some/full stall fractions 0.0, wal_sync 0/s and checkpoint write/sync time 0; the WAL pipeline has no queue to relieve and this transaction class is read-only, so the mean should not move by 0.5ms.

The wal_wait alert rests on one instantaneous sample (median 0.0, p95 0.0, max 1 of ~9 backends over 149 samples) against 0.00745 WAL writes per client transaction; no query_execution reconfiguration targets a waiter at the noise floor, so the max should not rise by 1 or more backends.

alternatives.statement: The GetUserTweets p99 tail (2626us vs p50 166us) is per-query JIT compilation / executor startup overhead introduced by jit=on, and would collapse if jit were disabled.

The rare wall-clock maxima (InsertTweet max 37428us, GetUserTweets max 31294us) are genuine intermittent storage fsync stalls that the wal_wait alert is detecting, and a storage-side change would remove them.

cross_domain_requirements: memory_storage: confirm no storage-side queue by holding write_average_ms / host_io stall fractions under observation rather than changing WAL knobs
concurrency_maintenance: confirm the read tail is not buffer-pin/LWLock contention via per-class wait-event sampling on the exact GetUserTweets SQL
why_exceeds_incumbent: It does not claim to exceed the incumbent. This is an observation-only proposal (knob_changes=[]): the verified incumbent is healthy (0 failed, 0 timeouts) and the dominant term is a fully-cached, optimal-plan, read-only index probe whose cost is count-driven, so any query_execution perturbation would be unfounded and would only consume the measurement budget. The proposal sharpens the diagnosis by freezing falsifiable no-change predictions on the read path and the WAL path.
